<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 47 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0ea93a5ced4a3eb3345ef7be27d1330f1b15c31e` — the merge of head `279bb7dca919e2b09539f9db8bf38ba9253b7df0` into base `d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0ea93a5ced4a3eb3345ef7be27d1330f1b15c31e && git checkout 0ea93a5ced4a3eb3345ef7be27d1330f1b15c31e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d 279bb7dca919e2b09539f9db8bf38ba9253b7df0 && git checkout -B drift-repro d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d && git merge --no-ff 279bb7dca919e2b09539f9db8bf38ba9253b7df0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d0512c2fbec9e0abd2f7fbd09986e4fdab73211d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `279bb7dca919e2b09539f9db8bf38ba9253b7df0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-crypto-provider-plugin-load-failure.integration.test.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-settings.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-detection.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/merge-boot-config.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts, packages/cli/package.json, packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-validator.zod.ts, docs/adr/0116-plugin-ordering-declared-contract.md, the contract-review record on PR #31263 (comment 6712974584, read for what each should-fix asked)

Inputs read: the PR body, file list, its one commit and message, and the net diff against `main` (merge-base `9447f9552`; `main` has since moved to `d0512c2fb`, with `serve.ts` byte-identical between the two and no commit since the base touching `packages/cli` or `packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts`), the check-runs on the head, the private drafter hand-back (its claims checked against the tree), the published spec and the cited code on `main`. No card, by the maintainer's ruling for this series; `Refs #28284` is the series mailbox, closed, with nothing on it about this PR. Why line, as fixed: 「QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)」. This PR is the follow-up to the #31263 review: its should-fix 2 (name a `devPlugins` entry by its own list), should-fix 3 (one reading of the declaration) and the docstring half of should-fix 1.

Check-runs on the head at the time of writing: 45 runs, 30 completed (17 `success`, 13 `skipped`, none failed or cancelled), 15 still in progress (seven `Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, the four `Type Check` jobs and three `Lint` jobs). Among the completed successes: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Test Core (5/8)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. The verdict below stands on the diff and the completed runs; the seat gates landing on the remaining runs finishing green, and a red run reopens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Which entries are refused does not move.** Right, verified in the tree rather than from the PR body: the predicate `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins` filters by is now the module-private `declaresCryptoProvider` (`providesServices` is an array naming `crypto-provider`), whose body is the same expression that was written inline on `main` both there and in `cryptoProviderPlugins`'s filter; what it is applied to (`said`: the materialized object, else the object entry, else nothing, which is refused) is unchanged. Every entry refused on `main` is refused on the head and the reverse. The PR's own agreement case pins that refusal and `cryptoProviderPlugins` answer alike for a declaring entry, an entry declaring another service and an entry declaring none.
2. **`refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins` is not routed through `cryptoProviderPlugins([said])`.** Right, and deliberately so: that routing would have changed which entries are refused (a loosening #31263's should-fix 3 did not ask for); the shared predicate gives the one reading without moving the set.
3. **A `devPlugins` entry is named `devPlugins[i]` under `--dev`.** Right. `UnloadedStackPlugin` gains an optional `list` (`'plugins' | 'devPlugins'`; absent reads as `plugins`), the label spells `${list}[${index}]`, and the boot loop records the list from two counts taken where the boot list is built: the authored `plugins` length (`stackBootPlugins(config, false)`) and the boot list's length (`stackBootPlugins(config, flags.dev)`), both read off the same `config` object at the same point. Between that point and the loop the only mutation of the list is one append (the runtime `AppPlugin` wrap), so every index below the boot count keeps its meaning and the half-open range between the two counts is exactly the `devPlugins` slice. Without `--dev` the two counts are equal and no entry takes the dev label. The appended wrap, if it ever failed to load, would carry the `plugins` label with an index past the authored list; it declares no `providesServices` and is an instance, so it is always ruled out and never named.
4. **The docstring states the rule the code applies.** Right: "refused when its `providesServices` names the provider, and ruled out when it declares other services or declares none", matching the code and the CONTROL pins, which is what #31263's should-fix 1 asked for; the PR body already said it.
5. **Order of events unchanged.** The record in the loop's catch still precedes `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins(unloadedStackPlugins)`, which still precedes the host provider construction; the source pin now anchors on `unloadedStackPlugins.push(` because the push became multi-line, and holds the same three positions.
6. **Public surface: unchanged.** `declaresCryptoProvider` is not exported; `UnloadedStackPlugin`'s new optional field sits on a type that `@objectstack/cli`'s export map (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `package.json`) does not reach.
7. **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** Right: nothing an author writes in metadata changes.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/cli`: patch.** Right: a user-visible refusal label and an internal refactor in a released package; a changeset is owed and `patch` is its level.
- **`Clause-②: no` — correctly `no`, not `no (narrowing)`.** No boot that succeeded before is refused now, and no boot refused before goes on now (① 1); the only observable change is the label text under `--dev`. The narrowing this family carries is the one #31263 declared and the record on that PR judged; this PR moves it by nothing. No published accept set or surface changes.
- **Changeset body.** Carries both declaration lines, the package and level, what the label changes to and the statement that the refused set is unchanged. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- **Disclosure check.** PR title and body (both languages), commit message, changeset, the new predicate's docblock, the rewritten docstring, the two new call-site comments, and both test files' headers and case names were read. All stay at the level of which entries are refused, which are not, where the check sits and what the refusal names; the one sentence on what the provider seals is `main`'s own text, unchanged. No breach.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Hand-back: the predicate is shared, not routed through `cryptoProviderPlugins([said])`, so the refused set does not move.** Confirmed and agreed (① 2).
- **Hand-back: the only mutation between the counts and the loop is the `AppPlugin` append; the appended wrap keeps the `plugins` label and declares nothing.** Confirmed in the tree (① 3): one append at the metadata-wrap site, no insertion, no reorder; the runtime `AppPlugin` declares `optionalDependencies` and `requiresServices` only.
- **Hand-back: the standalone-branch check is unchanged by this PR.** Confirmed. One observation for the series is recorded in the seat's private notes; it is not this PR's.
- **Hand-back verification claims** (red-first 2 failed / 32 passed against `main`'s blob, 34/34 restored, tsc 0, eslint 0, 72/72 derived gates, CLI suite green): consistent with my reading — the dev-label unit case and the `--dev` boot are the only assertions `main`'s label would fail; not reproduced (read-only); the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts.
- #31263's three should-fixes: closed (① 1, ① 3, ① 4). Its escalated items 1 and 2 are untouched by this PR and stay with their own private items.
- No open question in the hand-back is left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main` is #31263's, which the record on that PR judged: it takes no declared capability away at the consumer and makes the provider contract's own refusal real at the long-lived host. This PR changes nothing in that set (① 1) and was pushed on everything it does change: the shared predicate (identical body, identical operand, nameless candidates still refused), the label mapping (both counts from one `config` at one point; append-only mutation; `--dev` off collapses the range; a bare config under `--dev` maps the boot stack's list the same way; the appended wrap never reaches a label), the entries that fail before materializing (unchanged: refused by the specifier), the pin anchors (still in order), and the standalone-branch check (unchanged). No finding. No must-fix, no should-fix.
